newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia C.Bank to start selling 4-8 yr OFZ July 31. [CORRECTED 13:04 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russia C.Bank to start selling 4-8 yr OFZ July 31. [CORRECTED 13:04 GMT]

text.p: Russia will start offering a total 30.71 trillion roubles ($5.3 billion) in four- to eight-year OFZ government bonds on Thursday, the longest maturities for bonds issued by the Russian government so far, the central bank said on Wednesday.
"From tomorrow, the Central Bank of Russia will start selling OFZ bonds with 10-percent annual interest from its portfolio," deputy bank chairman Andrei Kozlov told Reuters.
The central bank will set the starting price of the bonds, which will be offered on the secondary market, based on an annual 17.5-percent yield, including accruals, Kozlov said.

"We have many bonds with a 10-percent coupon -- over 10 -- and from tomorrow, we will start to sell five of them," Kozlov said. "Our first starting quote for the sale, including accruals and discount, will be 17.5 percent."

He said the bonds, which were restructured from the Finance Ministry's long-term oustanding debts on March 15, 1997, have been held in the bank's portfolio since early this year. The central bank has about 13 bonds, all with maturities from four to 16 years, on its books.

"Yields have fallen enough to allow us to offer longer debt," Kozlov said. "In addition, investors have appeared, including non-residents, who are starting to be interested in longer-term investment."
